title: local OCI registry seeding + atomic promotion for air-gapped installs
author: Maya Singh
release_notes: Adds a vetted flow for seeding a local OCI registry with Redwood runtime and dependency artifacts, plus Terraform helpers and atomic promotion hooks for safe on-prem/air-gapped upgrades.
body: Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private in fully air-gapped/on-prem environments frequently ask for a repeatable, incremental way to populate a local OCI registry and perform zero-downtime upgrades by atomically promoting new index manifests. This PR introduces a seeding toolchain, a signed index format v2, Terraform helper modules to provision a local registry with ACLs, and installer hooks for atomic promotion and rollback. Summary of changes: 1) seedctl: a small Go tool that builds a minimal OCI index from a curated manifest, validates checksums and signatures, and uploads to a target registry using a resumable push protocol. 2) index-schema-v2: index manifests now include per-arch artifact metadata and a lightweight "seed policy" that allows selective seeding (runtime-only, runtime+charts, runtime+charts+debug). 3) terraform/registry-module: new module to create a small registry (harbor or distribution), set bucket-backed storage, configure pre-signed upload creds, and register an index promotion Lambda for on-prem platforms. 4) installer/hooks: preflight checks to ensure content-addressable layers are present, post-promotion hooks to update Helm repositories and local kubelet preloads, and a rollback hook that atomically switches the registry tag back to previous manifest. 5) docs and examples: step-by-step airgap seeding walkthroughs, example manifests for Alma/Rocky/Ubuntu, and a troubleshooting section for checksum mismatches. Checklist: - [x] seedctl CLI implemented with resumable pushes and signature verification - [x] index-schema-v2 definition and generator - [x] Terraform module + examples for local registry bootstrap - [x] installer preflight, promote, and rollback hooks wired into the airgap installer flow - [x] docs with step-by-step example and verification commands - [x] unit tests for index generator and promote/rollback state machine Usage notes: The seed manifest lets customers select a minimal surface area for their environment; by default seedctl will compute a compact "runtime-only" bundle that omits debug images and large optional tools. For incremental updates seedctl produces a delta index that only pushes changed blobs. The Terraform module provisions a registry and outputs a signed upload credential for use by seedctl. Upgrade flow: 1) seedctl --manifest v2 --mode promote push -> uploads delta content to local registry and prepares a signed index 2) Installer hooks validate checksums and warm the kubelet preloads 3) Atomic promotion step updates a registry-level pointer (OCI tag) to the new index 4) Health checks run against a small canary workload; if failures, rollback hook reverts pointer to previous index and prunes warm caches Testing performed: - unit tests for index creation and delta computation - integration run against a local distribution registry and Harbor 2.5 (CI-local) - manual upgrade / rollback on a 3-node k3s lab with Rocky Linux showing zero-app downtime for typical text-generation workloads Known limitations and future work: - image signing currently uses an injected keypair; we plan KMS/HSM integration for customers that require key custody - sparse index optimization for very large corp registries remains TODO - OCI mirror performance tuning for ppc64le/arm64 will be follow-ups Security notes: signature verification is enforced by default; seedctl supports an allowlist file for blobs when customers intentionally tolerate checksum mismatches for transient mirrors. Backwards compatibility: index v2 is backward compatible with the runtime; seedctl emits a compatibility flag and the installer will fall back to index-v1 parsing when needed.
commit_summary: feat(seedctl): implement resumable push and delta index generation
feat(index): add index-schema-v2 and generator utility
feat(terraform): new module registry-local with harbor/distribution examples
chore(installer): wire promote/rollback hooks into airgap flow
docs: airgap seeding walkthrough and troubleshooting
review_comments: Ethan Novak: Can seedctl handle partial network failures and resume uploads? Please add tests that simulate an interrupted upload and resume the push.
Maya Singh (reply): Yes — resumable uploads are implemented. Added unit test run that simulates a broken stream and resumes. See tests/integration/seedctl_local_registry_test.go.
Priya Shah: Terraform module should expose a lean option for constrained air-gapped sites (no harbor, just distribution). Add examples and document storage backends.
Maya Singh (reply): Added distribution example and documented S3 vs filesystem backends. Also added input variable `lean_mode` to toggle harbor vs distribution.

Luca Moretti: Is the promote operation atomic on both Harbor and Docker distribution? We need to ensure pointer update does not cause a half-baked state where some nodes see new index and others don't.

Maya Singh (reply): Promote uses an OCI tag swap backed by registry transactions where available; for distribution-based registries we use a two-phase rename + health-check with prewarm step to ensure blobs are present on all mirrors before switching. Documented behavior in seeding.md.
manual_test_steps: 3) run installer with --airgap-registry registry.local:5000 and observe preflight successes
4) trigger promote via installer UI or CLI and validate canaries
5) if canaries fail, run installer --rollback and verify registry pointer reverted
notes: After merging we scheduled a follow-up to add KMS-backed key storage (ENG-4185) and arm64/power optimizations (ENG-4210).
